evidence_status: Established platform and institutional evidence; causal vote effect unproven
mechanisms: Coordinated promotion, recommender amplification, opaque sponsorship, cross-platform operation
observed_or_prospective_harm: Information-integrity crisis, institutional response, annulment controversy, and legitimacy damage
missing_failed_controls: Sponsor transparency, earlier network detection, auditable recommender risk, evidence preservation
priority_lesson: Do not infer result causality from virality; map controller, distribution, evidence, and institutional consequences.

observed_or_prospective_harm: High response burden, trust erosion, and vulnerability to opaque external control
missing_failed_controls: Cross-platform coordination, financial attribution, rapid evidence and public communication
priority_lesson: AI is an enabling layer inside a broader influence system, not a standalone cause.

evidence_status: Synthetic-audio incident widely documented; effect on outcome unproven
mechanisms: Late-cycle synthetic audio, authenticity uncertainty, compressed correction window
observed_or_prospective_harm: Epistemic uncertainty and response difficulty close to voting
missing_failed_controls: Fast authentication, candidate verification, trusted channels, proportional correction
priority_lesson: The democratic harm can be uncertainty and institutional overload even without measurable persuasion.

election_incident_domain: Brazil general election, 2026 — TSE implementation regime
evidence_status: Binding Resolution and Portaria adopted; plans due 2026-08-16; election and causal effects not yet observable as of 2026-08-11
mechanisms: AI assistants, synthetic media, recommender systems, boosted political content, rapid incident response
observed_or_prospective_harm: Prospective risk; no 2026 voting outcome yet
missing_failed_controls: Independent baseline, plan-quality audit, exposure data, assistant-neutrality tests, appeal testing and post-election causal design
timing: Plans by 2026-08-16; first round 2026-10-04; possible second round 2026-10-25; consolidated reports by 2026-12-19
priority_lesson: Treat as a prospective implementation study. Plan completion is not effectiveness, and virality is not evidence of changed votes.

evidence_status: Established data-governance and campaign-infrastructure case; individual persuasion effects contested
mechanisms: Data extraction, profiling, targeted messaging, opaque controller networks
observed_or_prospective_harm: Loss of informational autonomy, accountability failure, and trust damage
missing_failed_controls: Data minimization, sponsor/targeting transparency, researcher access, functional exit
priority_lesson: The strongest evidence concerns data and governance failure, not deterministic mind control.
sources: Regulatory and parliamentary records; see Evidence Ledger

observed_or_prospective_harm: Potential misregistration, misdirection, or reduced participation

election_incident_domain: Legitimate synthetic media in election communication
mechanisms: Translation, accessibility, parody, low-cost outreach, candidate-authorized synthetic speech
observed_or_prospective_harm: No inherent harm; risk arises from deception, attribution failure, or discriminatory enforcement
missing_failed_controls: Clear authorization and provenance; contextual exceptions; appeal
priority_lesson: A blanket synthetic-media ban would sacrifice speech and access without addressing interactive manipulation.
sources: International IDEA and election-regulator guidance; see Evidence Ledger

election_incident_domain: Public authority dependence on proprietary AI vendors
evidence_status: Structural risk with operational precedents; democratic effects under-measured
mechanisms: Vendor lock-in, deskilling, opaque updates, cloud-model integration, weak exit
observed_or_prospective_harm: Reduced institutional autonomy, continuity, contestability, and public accountability
missing_failed_controls: Public registers, multi-provider architecture, tested exit, internal expertise, contractual audit
priority_lesson: Agency transfer can occur inside institutions even without manipulative content.
sources: Canada, UK, EU procurement, and OECD materials; see Evidence Ledger
